title: Headings & Paragraphs 📝
description: Organize text with heading levels and paragraphs.

slides.title: Headings: Your Content’s Signposts 🪧
slides.content:
# The `<h1>` to `<h6>` Tags

HTML provides six levels of headings:
- `<h1>` is the most important (usually the page title).
- `<h2>` for major sections.
- `<h3>` for subsections, and so on down to `<h6>`.

Search engines use headings to understand page structure. Never skip levels (e.g., h1 directly to h3) – keep a logical hierarchy.

quizData.question: Which heading tag should you use for the main title of a page?
quizData.explanation: <h1> is the top‑level heading and should be used for the primary title, with lower levels for sub‑sections.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## One <h1> per page

For SEO and accessibility, it's best practice to have a single `<h1>` that describes the page's main topic. Use `<h2>` and lower for all other headings.
